Cli_Help:
{0} {1} - application packaging for Microsoft Intune (built on PSAppDeployToolkit)

Usage:
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe [file]
      Opens a project (project.json) or analyses an installer (.msi / .exe).
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --build <project.json|installer> [--out <folder>] [--native]
      Builds a package without opening the window. --native forces the built-in packager.
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --setup
      Downloads and verifies the dependencies (database, PSAppDeployToolkit, IntuneWinAppUtil).
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --update-catalog [--force]
      Updates the application database.
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --sandbox <package folder>
      Tests a generated package in Windows Sandbox: installs it and runs the detection rule.
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --install [--desktop-shortcut] [--quiet]
      Installs for the current user (Start menu and Installed apps). No administrator rights needed.
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --uninstall [--purge] [--quiet]
      Removes the installation. --purge also removes settings and downloaded tools.
  J365.IntunePSApp.exe --update [--check]
      Updates this executable to the latest release (--check only tells whether there is a newer one).

Options:
  --lang <en|pt-BR>   Interface language for this run.
  --version           Shows the version.
  --help              Shows this help.

Publish_IntroInApp: The package goes to Microsoft Graph with the connection of this computer: the app, its icon, detection, requirements and the encrypted content. Nothing is installed on this computer and no password or secret is stored. If something fails after the app was created, the incomplete app is removed.

Diag_Intro: Microsoft Graph accepted the connection, but Intune refused the request. Check, in this order:

Diag_RoleMissing: An Intune role must be active for your account now: Intune Administrator or Global Administrator (or an Intune role that manages apps). With PIM, activate it and try again a minute later.

Diag_PlanNone: The tenant {0} has no Microsoft Intune subscription (checked on {1}), and without it Intune refuses every request, whatever the connection. An administrator activates Microsoft Intune Plan 1, or its free trial, in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Marketplace); then publish again.
Diag_PlanBasic: The tenant {0} only has Basic Mobility and Security, which comes with Microsoft 365 and does not deploy Win32 apps (checked on {1}). Publishing needs Microsoft Intune Plan 1 (alone, or in Microsoft 365 Business Premium, E3 or E5).
Diag_PlanInactive: The Microsoft Intune subscription of the tenant {0} expired or was suspended (checked on {1}): a trial that ended gives this answer. An administrator renews it, or activates Microsoft Intune Plan 1, in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Diag_PlanActiveWait: The tenant has Microsoft Intune and the application has the permission: a permission or a subscription activated a moment ago takes a while to reach Intune (sometimes an hour). Try again later.

Plan_HowToInactive:
How to fix it:
1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, Billing > Your products shows Microsoft Intune Plan 1 (or the suite that included it) and its status. A paid subscription is reactivated or bought there (Reactivate in Microsoft 365).
2. A trial that ended usually cannot start again: buy Intune, or start the trial of another product that includes it (Microsoft 365 Business Premium, E3 or E5, or EMS E3/E5) in the Marketplace.
3. Then click Check again: Intune answers a few minutes after it is active. For the devices to receive the app, their users also need an Intune license.
Plan_HowToNone:
How to fix it:
1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, Marketplace: buy Microsoft Intune Plan 1 or start its free trial, or a product that includes it (Microsoft 365 Business Premium, E3 or E5, or EMS E3/E5).
2. Then click Check again: Intune answers a few minutes after it is active. For the devices to receive the app, their users also need an Intune license.

Ed_RemovePrevHint: Uninstall first (when something is installed), install after. Inside the package the detection rule is not consulted, so the same version is replaced as well and two versions never stay side by side. With the package mark (Detection step), Intune also runs the package where the application was installed some other way.
Ed_KeepNewer: Keep a newer version that is already installed
Ed_KeepNewerHint: When the device already has a newer version (the app updated itself, for example), the package does not downgrade it: it only records the package mark, so Intune reports the app as installed.
Ed_ConfirmDiscard: The open package ({0}) has changes that were not saved or generated. Discard them?
Ed_ExistingTitle: Versions already installed on the device
Ed_ExistingFlowOn: Order on the device: 1) closes the application, 2) uninstalls every version found (MSI and EXE), 3) installs the new one. No detection runs before uninstalling.
Ed_PatternOthers: In the database, "{0}" also matches: {1}. Where one of them is installed, it would be uninstalled before the installation and would count for the detection rule. Make the name more specific if you can.
Ed_ExistingFlowOff: Nothing is uninstalled: the installer runs over whatever is there, which can leave two versions of the same application.
Ed_PatternHint: Use * as a wildcard: 7-Zip* finds "7-Zip 24.08 (x64)" and "7-Zip 26.06 (x64)". Avoid generic names.
Ed_InstalledFound: {0} program(s) on this computer match '{1}' and would be removed.

Ed_UninstallArgsHint: MSI is removed automatically (msiexec /x). For .exe type the switch (for example /S, /VERYSILENT). Empty: only programs with a registered silent uninstall are removed.
Ed_UninstallByCode: This .exe installs the MSI product {0}: the uninstall removes it by that product code (msiexec /x), so no switches are needed here. The name above still removes other versions.

Ed_DetMarkOffHint: Off: any copy that matches the rule counts as installed, even one installed some other way. Intune does not run the package on those computers and that copy is not removed.
Ed_DetectedNoMark: The application is installed on this computer, but not by this package (no mark in {0}): Intune would run the package here, remove the copy found and install this version. This is the expected result where the package has not run yet.

Ed_TestStarted: Test started. Logs in C:\Windows\Logs\Software or in the Intune logs folder.
Ed_TestCancelled: Test cancelled (administrator permission was not granted).
Ed_SandboxTip: Opens Windows Sandbox (a disposable Windows), installs the package and runs the detection rule. Nothing changes on this computer.
Ed_SandboxUnsupported:
Windows Sandbox does not exist in this edition of Windows.

It is part of Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise and Education (not Home, not Windows Server). Use "Test installation" on a test computer or in a virtual machine.
Ed_SandboxNotEnabled:
Windows Sandbox is not enabled on this computer.

It is an optional Windows feature ("Windows Sandbox", Containers-DisposableClientVM) that has to be installed once. The application can install it now: Windows asks for administrator permission and the computer must be restarted afterwards.

To do it yourself: "Turn Windows features on or off" > Windows Sandbox.
Ed_SandboxVirtualization: Note: hardware virtualisation looks disabled in the firmware (BIOS/UEFI) of this computer. Windows Sandbox only starts with Intel VT-x / AMD-V enabled.
Ed_SandboxEnabled:
The Windows Sandbox feature was installed.

Restart the computer to finish, then click "Test in Sandbox" again.
Ed_SandboxEnableFailed:
Windows could not install the feature (DISM code {0}).

Try "Turn Windows features on or off" > Windows Sandbox, and check that virtualisation is enabled in the firmware (BIOS/UEFI).
Ed_SandboxEnableCancelled: The feature was not installed: administrator permission was not granted.
Ed_SandboxRunning:
Windows Sandbox is already open, and Windows allows only one at a time.

Close the Windows Sandbox window and click "Test in Sandbox" again.
Ed_SandboxStarted: Windows Sandbox is starting. The package is installed and checked automatically in its PowerShell window; the result also appears here.
Ed_SandboxWaiting: Windows Sandbox is open: waiting for the result of the test. The first start takes about a minute.
Ed_SandboxClosed: Windows Sandbox was closed before the test reported a result.
Ed_SandboxResultOk: Sandbox, {0}: passed. Exit code {1}, detection rule: {2} ({3} s).
Ed_SandboxResultFail: Sandbox, {0}: failed. Exit code {1}, detection rule: {2}. Open the logs to see why.
Ed_PublishCalloutConnected: Connected as {0} · tenant {1}. The app, its icon, detection, requirements and content go to Intune in one step.
Ed_PublishCalloutNoPlan: Connected as {0} · tenant {1}, which has no active Microsoft Intune subscription: Intune refuses the publication until an administrator activates it.
Ed_PublishCalloutNotConnected: Connect to Intune once (automatic setup, with an app certificate or your account) and publish from here.
Ed_PublishAfterBuildTip: Opens the publication as soon as the package is generated.
Ed_PublishTip: Creates or updates the app in your tenant through Microsoft Graph, with the certificate of this computer or your own sign-in. By default the app is created without assignments.
Ed_PublishStarted: Follow the PowerShell window to sign in and publish. The result appears here when it finishes.
Publish_IfExists: If an app with this name already exists
Publish_ExistsAsk: Ask: show the Intune apps with this name first
Publish_ExistsUpdate: Update the existing app (new content and settings; assignments are kept)
Publish_ExistsNew: Create another app with the same name
Publish_AssignNone: None: I will assign it in Intune later (recommended)
Publish_AssignRequiredGroup: Required for a group (installs by itself)
Publish_AssignRequiredUsers: Required for all users (installs by itself)
Publish_AssignRequiredDevices: Required for all devices (installs by itself)
Publish_AssignHint: The assignment is only applied to a new app. Start with a pilot group.
Publish_Group: Object ID of the group (Entra ID)
Publish_InvalidGroup: Enter the object ID of the group (GUID). It is shown on the page of the group in Entra ID.
Publish_InvalidAssignment: Intune does not allow "available" for all devices. Choose all users or a group.
Publish_ConfirmBroad:
This assignment installs the application automatically in the WHOLE tenant, with no pilot group.
